title: Espaces stratifiés et voisinages côniques (ou : déploiement des espaces stratifiés) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: notes on stratified spaces and conic neighbourhoods, toward the 'déploiement' (unfolding) of a stratified space. The space X has closed strata X_i indexed by a poset I. It also carries auxiliary data (B_α, Σ_α), α ∈ R (on the next page α ∈ Λ). These look like subspaces with boundary or marking data, which conic neighbourhoods must be transversal to. The previous page added the axiom X_i ∩ X_j = ∪_{h ≤ i,j} X_h.

Step 1. Let I_0 be the set of minimal elements of I. Take a strict conic neighbourhood T_{I_0} = ∐_{β∈I_0} T_β of X_{I_0}. Assume:
- it is strictly transversal to the (B_α, Σ_α);
- each X_i with i ∈ I* := I \ I_0 is strictly admissible for T_{I_0}. Admissible means X_i ∩ T_β is the conic neighbourhood induced over X_i ∩ X_β.

Step 2, formula (14). For β minimal, the axiom gives X_i ∩ X_β = ∪_{h ≤ i, h ≤ β} X_h. The only h ≤ β is β itself. So the intersection is X_β if i ≥ β and empty otherwise.

Step 3. Let I_β = {i : i > β}; it lies in I* by minimality.
- (15): for i ∈ I* \ I_β, X_i ∩ T_β = ∅, by admissibility and X_i ∩ X_β = ∅.
- (16): for i ∈ I_β, X_i ⊃ X_β.
- (16'): X_i ∩ T_β = I·(X_i ∩ Ṫ_β) ∪ X_β. That is, the trace of X_i on the cone is the mapping cylinder of p_β restricted to the link-stratum Ẋ_i = X_i ∩ Ṫ_β, with its base X_β.

Step 4, conclusion (17). The whole system (X, (X_i), (B_α, Σ_α), (T_β)) is determined by smaller data:
- the 'cut' space X* = X \ T°_{I_0}, with boundary pieces Ẋ_β = Ṫ_β;
- the traces B*_α, Σ*_α, X*_i on X*;
- the minimal strata X_β with their induced data;
- the projections p_β : Ẋ_β → X_β.

The reconstruction is X = X* ∪_{Ẋ} C(p), where C(p) is the mapping cylinder. A first crossed-out draft of (18) appears here; the next page makes it precise as a 'système de cylindres-bord transversaux' and states the transversality conditions (20).

Purpose: one inductive step of unfolding. Removing open conic neighbourhoods of the minimal strata turns a stratified space into a stratified space with boundary plus fibrations over lower strata. Iterating should give an equivalence between stratified spaces with conic structure and systems of 'manifolds with boundary/corners + cylinder data'.
errors: No genuine error. (14) is cited ('en vertu de (14)') a line before it is written, but it follows correctly from the axiom X_i ∩ X_j = ∪_{h≤i,j} X_h of the previous page plus minimality of β.
The notation 'I.(X_i ∩ Ṫ_β) ∪ X_β' in (16') is shorthand. Strictly, it should be the mapping cylinder C(p_β|Ẋ_i), with X_β glued via p_β, not a disjoint product with an interval.
Implicit hypothesis: (16') needs 'admissible' to mean that X_i ∩ T_β is exactly the restriction of the conic structure, i.e. a union of fibres of the cone projection. This is not stated on the page.

ideas.what: Lattice-type axiom for closed strata, X_i ∩ X_j = ∪_{h≤i,j} X_h. For a minimal stratum it gives X_i ∩ X_β = X_β or ∅.
ideas.usually_credited_to: Whitney, Thom, Mather (frontier condition); modern poset-stratified formalism (Lurie, Higher Algebra appendix A)

ideas.what: Cutting out open conic neighbourhoods of the minimal strata and recovering X as the pushout X* ∪_{Ẋ} C(p) along mapping cylinders of the link projections.
ideas.modern_name: unfolding / resolution ('unzipping') of stratified spaces; Thom–Mather control data; mapping-cylinder neighbourhoods
ideas.usually_credited_to: Thom (1969), Mather (1970), Goresky (abstract stratified sets), Verona, Quinn; Ayala–Francis–Tanaka (2017, unzipping of conically smooth stratified spaces)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984), §5–6, on stratified spaces, tame topology and 'déploiement'

ideas.what: Keeping track of auxiliary transversal data (B_α, Σ_α) and of the higher strata (via admissibility) during the cutting procedure.
ideas.modern_name: transversality of conic/tubular neighbourhoods to substrata; systems of manifolds with corners

missed.claim: This is a concrete fragment of the inductive step of Grothendieck's 'déploiement' programme from Esquisse §5–6. The extra transversal data (B_α, Σ_α) are carried along and reconstructed. It closely prefigures the 'unzipping' equivalence of Ayala–Francis–Tanaka, but contains no result beyond what is now standard.
missed.quote: Ainsi, le système (X, (X_i)_{i∈I}, (B_α, E_α)_{α∈R}, (T_β)_{β∈I_0}) se reconstitue à l'aide de (X_β)_{β∈I_0}, ...
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Mainly historical. It documents that Grothendieck in 1981–82 worked out the reconstruction of a stratified space from the cut space plus cylinder data, with transversality bookkeeping. This is rarely cited in the AFT / Lurie stratified literature.

deep.surprise_reason: A routine, correct inductive step: removing conic neighbourhoods of minimal strata and reconstructing via mapping cylinders. The idea is known (Thom–Mather, Goresky, later AFT) and is already announced by Grothendieck in Esquisse d'un programme. Interesting only as a working detail of the déploiement programme.
transcription_corrections: Line 2–3: '(B_i,E_i)' should be the auxiliary data, written (B_α, E_α) or (B_α, Σ_α) to match (17) and the next page. The manuscript symbol is ambiguous.
'supposons le stat[?] transversal' most likely reads 'supposons le str. transversal' (strictement transversal).
In (14), the second case reads roughly 'X_β sinon, i.e. si i ≥ β (car ...)'; the parenthetical justification is illegible, and 'contient' is a guess.
Line 1: 'voisin.' is written in full, 'voisinage'; 'tubulaire' is crossed out and replaced by 'cônique'.
In (17), the index set is written 'α∈R'; the next page uses Λ.
